verdict: Alex is a credible platform PM with directly relevant internal-API and developer-customer experience, plus the consulting background this role lists as a nice-to-have. The blocker is the one hard requirement with no supporting evidence: hands-on experience shipping LLM or ML-powered products — a GenAI prioritization framework built as a consultant is strategy work, not shipping, so this is a stretch application that hinges on how literally the hiring team reads that requirement.

strong_matches.skill: 4+ years of product management experience on technical or platform products
strong_matches.evidence: Big Bank Co. — Product Manager, Payments Platform since 2022 owning an internal payments API, plus Founding PM at Early Startup 2020–2022, giving roughly five years of PM experience, most of it on platform/technical products.

strong_matches.skill: Experience working closely with engineering on APIs or developer-facing products
strong_matches.evidence: At Big Bank Co., led the roadmap for an internal payments API consumed by 12 product teams and partnered with 20 engineers to cut integration time from 6 weeks to 2.

strong_matches.skill: Run customer discovery with internal product teams and turn it into requirements
strong_matches.evidence: At Early Startup, ran 30+ customer discovery interviews to define the MVP; at Big Bank Co., the internal API's 12 consuming product teams were effectively the internal customer base for roadmap decisions.

strong_matches.skill: Comfortable writing SQL and defining adoption metrics
strong_matches.evidence: At Big Bank Co., built SQL dashboards tracking API adoption and error rates — the same adoption/quality metric pattern this role asks for.

strong_matches.skill: Serving internal teams as customers / balancing competing internal needs
strong_matches.evidence: At Big Bank Co., prioritized a single internal payments API roadmap across 12 product teams with differing needs.
Consultant at a Strategy Consulting Firm 2017–2020, including a GenAI use-case prioritization framework for a Fortune 100 retailer.
Founding PM at Early Startup: took a B2B scheduling product from zero to 40 paying customers.

skill_gaps.skill: Hands-on experience shipping LLM- or ML-powered products
skill_gaps.why_it_matters: The entire platform exists to help teams ship LLM features, so the PM needs lived experience with model behavior, latency, cost and failure modes rather than a consulting-level view of use cases.

skill_gaps.skill: Model evaluation and AI safety work with data science and legal
skill_gaps.why_it_matters: A named responsibility of the role, and the resume shows no partnership with data science, legal, risk or compliance on model quality or safety.

skill_gaps.skill: Running experiments and interpreting A/B test results
skill_gaps.why_it_matters: The role requires defining success metrics and running experiments; the resume shows dashboards and reporting but no evidence of designing or reading out a controlled experiment.

skill_gaps.skill: Evaluation frameworks for AI systems (evals, golden datasets, quality scoring)
skill_gaps.why_it_matters: Listed as a nice-to-have, but it's how an AI platform PM proves 'quality' is improving and would meaningfully offset the missing LLM shipping experience.

skill_gaps.skill: Demonstrated written communication to senior leadership
skill_gaps.why_it_matters: The role explicitly calls for communicating priorities and tradeoffs to senior leadership, and the resume never mentions executive-facing docs, strategy narratives or reviews.

why_youre_a_fit: You already do the core job in a different domain: at Big Bank Co. you own an internal platform API whose customers are 12 internal product teams — structurally identical to owning an internal AI platform serving product teams.

You have a hard, defensible platform outcome — cutting integration time from 6 weeks to 2 with 20 engineers — which is exactly the 'ship safely and quickly' promise this AI platform is making to its internal users.
Your SQL dashboards on API adoption and error rates map directly to the role's ask to define success metrics for adoption and quality.
Your 30+ discovery interviews at Early Startup prove you can turn unstructured user conversations into requirements, which is the discovery motion this role wants applied to internal teams.

Your consulting work included a GenAI use-case prioritization framework for a Fortune 100 retailer, so you can speak the language of AI prioritization and tradeoffs even if you haven't shipped the underlying models.
Founding PM experience taking a product from zero to 40 paying customers signals you can stand up a platform offering that doesn't yet have adoption.
what_to_emphasize: Owning an internal API platform for 12 consuming product teams — lead with this; it is the closest analog to the job and the strongest single argument.
The 6-weeks-to-2-weeks integration time reduction with 20 engineers, framed as developer experience and time-to-ship for internal builders.
SQL dashboards on adoption and error rates, framed as defining and instrumenting platform success and quality metrics.

The GenAI use-case prioritization framework for a Fortune 100 retailer — position it as evaluating and prioritizing AI use cases against feasibility and risk, but be honest in interviews that it was advisory, not shipped.
30+ customer discovery interviews as the method you'd use on internal product teams in the first 90 days.
Zero-to-one credibility from Early Startup for a platform that still has to earn internal adoption.

skills_to_build.how: Build and ship something small but real that calls an LLM API — e.g. a retrieval-backed internal tool — and be able to talk specifically about prompt iteration, latency, cost per call and failure handling in an interview.

Create an eval set for your side project: define 30–50 test cases with expected behavior, score outputs, and track quality across prompt or model changes so you can describe an evals-driven release process.
Take a short course on experiment design (sample size, significance, guardrail metrics) and prepare a story about how you would have A/B tested the payments API adoption work you already led.

skills_to_build.skill: AI safety, policy and legal partnership
skills_to_build.how: Read your target company's published AI principles plus a standard framework like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and prepare a point of view on how you'd gate an internal LLM launch with legal and data science.
Write a one-to-two page AI platform strategy memo for Example Corp — internal customer segments, adoption metrics, safety guardrails — and offer it as a work sample with your application.
